# Claim producer

A claim producer hands a node exclusive access to something outside rimsky — a table, a folder, a capacity counter — and closes that access when the node settles. Rimsky calls `Open` before it dispatches the node and one terminal verb after.

Two services make up the guide. `ClaimProducer` carries the acquisition verbs. `ClaimProducerObservability` carries the operator read surface, and you serve it from the same process. Implement `ClaimProducer` alone and rimsky still acquires claims through you.

Proto files: `claim_producer.proto`, `claim_producer_observability.proto`.

## The RPCs

| RPC | Required |
| --- | --- |
| `ClaimProducer.Capabilities(CapabilitiesRequest) → CapabilitiesResponse` | Yes |
| `ClaimProducer.Open(OpenRequest) → OpenResponse` | Yes |
| `ClaimProducer.Commit(CommitRequest) → CommitResponse` | Yes |
| `ClaimProducer.Abandon(AbandonRequest) → AbandonResponse` | Yes |
| `ClaimProducer.Release(ReleaseRequest) → ReleaseResponse` | Yes |
| `ClaimProducer.SplitScope(SplitScopeRequest) → SplitScopeResponse` | Only when you advertise it |
| `ClaimProducer.ScopesConflict(ClaimScopesConflictRequest) → ScopesConflictResponse` | Only when you advertise it |
| `ClaimProducerObservability.Capabilities(GetClaimProducerCapabilitiesRequest) → ClaimProducerObservabilityCapabilities` | Only with the observability sibling |
| `ClaimProducerObservability.GetClaim(GetClaimRequest) → ClaimDetail` | Only when you advertise it |
| `ClaimProducerObservability.StreamClaim(StreamClaimRequest) → stream ClaimEvent` | Only when you advertise it |
| `ClaimProducerObservability.ListClaims(ListClaimsRequest) → ClaimList` | Only when you advertise it |
| `ClaimProducerObservability.GetAdminView(GetAdminViewRequest) → AdminView` | Only when you declare views |

## Advertising yourself

Rimsky calls `ClaimProducer.Capabilities` at startup and serves what you return at `GET /v1/observability/claim-producers`. What you put in the handshake is what the operator sees.

`CapabilitiesResponse` fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `write_semantics_allowed` | The envelope of semantics you may realize. Must be non-empty. |
| `supports_split_scope` | Whether you implement `SplitScope` |
| `supports_scopes_conflict` | Whether you implement `ScopesConflict` |
| `protocols` | The mix-in protocols you also serve |
| `validation_supported_roles` | The roles you answer on the `Validation` mix-in |
| `declared_error_classes` | The error-class vocabulary template authors may route on |

`WriteSemantics` takes five values: `WRITE_SEMANTICS_UNKNOWN`, `WRITE_SEMANTICS_SYNC`, `WRITE_SEMANTICS_STAGED_ASYNC`, `WRITE_SEMANTICS_BLOCKING_ASYNC`, `WRITE_SEMANTICS_READ_ONLY`. Advertise the concrete four you can realize; never advertise `UNKNOWN`.

An operator repeats your envelope in the deployment's `claim_producers.<name>.write_semantics_allowed`. Every value the operator declares must appear in the set you advertise. Rimsky checks this at startup and refuses to start on a mismatch, naming both sets.

`protocols` accepts `data_processing`, `validation`, `lifecycle_subscriber`, and `executor`. Advertise `data_processing` when you also serve the `DataProcessing` service; rimsky checks that you actually serve it.

## Open

`Open` acquires the claim. Rimsky calls it before dispatching the node.

`OpenRequest` fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `claim_id` | Rimsky's id for this claim |
| `producer_name` | The name the deployment declared you under |
| `selector` | What to acquire, already resolved against the instance's parameters |
| `intent` | `r` for read, `rw` for read-write |
| `alias` | The template's name for this claim, and the key you appear under in the dispatch |
| `template_id` | The template hash |
| `instance_id` | The instance |
| `run_scope_id` | The execution context |
| `lifetime` | `subgraph` or `durable` |
| `data` | The template author's opaque blob, byte-for-byte |

The selector arrives concrete: the template declares a placeholder and you receive the resolved value. Read `data` as your own configuration channel — rimsky passes it through untouched.

`OpenResponse` is a oneof over two cases.

**`Acquired`** means you have it.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `address` | Where the thing is. Reaches the node's attributes. |
| `payload` | What the node needs to work with it. Reaches the node's attributes. |
| `claim_scope` | Opaque bytes identifying what you acquired |
| `realized_write_semantics` | The concrete semantics this claim got |

All three byte fields reach the executor through the dispatch's claim-producer handle map. That is how store-specific detail — a connection string, a staging location, a row payload — reaches the executor without the template author knowing anything about your store.

`realized_write_semantics` must be concrete and must be a member of the envelope you advertised. Returning `UNKNOWN`, or a value outside the envelope, fails the acquisition.

`claim_scope` identifies the thing acquired, so two `Open` calls with the same selector must produce byte-equal scopes, and byte-equal scopes must carry the same realized semantics.

**`Unavailable`** means you refuse.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `error_class` | Why you refused |

Your class reaches the template as the node's error class, so a template can route on the specific reason you refused. Rimsky falls back to the synthetic class `acquire/unavailable` when you leave it empty. An RPC error rather than an `Unavailable` result falls back to `acquire/producer_error`.

## The terminal verbs

Rimsky calls exactly one terminal verb per claim, after the node settles.

| Verb | When rimsky calls it |
| --- | --- |
| `Commit` | The node succeeded and the claim should be promoted |
| `Abandon` | The node failed and the claim's work should be dropped |
| `Release` | The claim should be let go without promoting or dropping |

All three take `claim_id`, `claim_scope`, `address`, and `lease_token`. `CommitResponse` returns `version_id` and `producer_metadata`; the other two return empty messages.

**All three must be idempotent.** Rimsky retries a terminal verb when an acknowledgement is lost, and a redelivery that corrupts your state is a conformance failure. Answer a duplicate `Commit`, `Abandon`, or `Release` on the same claim the same way you answered the first.

## SplitScope

`SplitScope` partitions one claim into sub-claims, so a node can fan out one child execution per partition. Implement it only if your store has partitions worth fanning out over, and advertise `supports_split_scope` when you do.

`SplitScopeRequest` carries `claim_handle_id` and an opaque `partition_request` the template author wrote.

`SplitScopeResponse` returns a list of `SubScopeDescriptor`, each with `claim_scope_data`, `partition_key`, `producer_metadata`, `address`, `payload`, and `lease_token`.

Return one descriptor per element of the request, preserving each element's partition key and payload. Leave `address` empty on the descriptors; rimsky fills it from the parent claim.

Answer `SplitScope` with an error when you do not support it, and leave `supports_split_scope` false.

## ScopesConflict

`ScopesConflict` answers whether two claim scopes overlap, so rimsky can tell whether two nodes are competing. It takes `claim_scope_a` and `claim_scope_b` and returns a single `conflicts` boolean.

Advertise `supports_scopes_conflict` when you implement it. When you do not, rimsky falls back to byte equality: two scopes conflict when their bytes match exactly.

## The observability sibling

Rimsky calls `ClaimProducerObservability.Capabilities` against the declared `claim_producers.<name>.observability_endpoint` at startup, and serves what you return on its observability read routes.

`ClaimProducerObservabilityCapabilities` fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `supports_claim_get` | Whether you answer `GetClaim` |
| `supports_claim_stream` | Whether you answer `StreamClaim` |
| `supports_list_claims` | Whether you answer `ListClaims` |
| `retention_after_terminal_seconds` | How long you keep a claim after it closes |
| `custom_ui` | A URL and embed mode an operator dashboard can link or frame |
| `admin_views` | Named views an operator can request through `GetAdminView` |
| `http_bridge_url` | Recorded and republished. Rimsky never dials it. |

`GetClaim` returns a `ClaimDetail`: `claim_id`, `state`, `address`, `payload`, `scope`, `opened_at`, `closed_at`, and a `history` of `ClaimEvent`. `ClaimState` takes `CLAIM_STATE_UNSPECIFIED`, `OPEN`, `COMMITTED`, `ABANDONED`, `RELEASED`, and `UNKNOWN`. Answer a claim you have never seen, or one whose retention window has passed, with state `UNKNOWN`.

`StreamClaim` streams `ClaimEvent` values for one claim. Each event carries `event_id`, `parent_event_id`, `timestamp`, `severity`, `category`, `message`, and an `attributes` struct. Give every event a non-empty `event_id`.

`ListClaims` takes `state_filter`, `cursor`, and `limit`, and returns `ClaimSummary` rows plus a `next_cursor`. Honour `limit`: returning more rows than asked for is a conformance failure.

`GetAdminView` takes a `view_name` and a `params` struct, and returns an `AdminView` with a column `schema`, a `data` struct, and a `render_hint`. Declare each view up front in `admin_views` as an `AdminViewDecl` with a `name`, `title`, `description`, and typed `params`, each param marked `required` or not.

## The HTTP+JSON bridge

`serverkit.Mount` mounts the seven producer verbs on a `http.ServeMux` as `POST /v1/capabilities`, `/v1/open`, `/v1/commit`, `/v1/abandon`, `/v1/release`, `/v1/split_scope`, and `/v1/scopes_conflict`. `serverkit.MountObservability` mounts the observability reads under `/observability/v1/`.

Rimsky dials claim producers over gRPC only — `claim_producers.<name>.endpoint` must use the `grpc://` scheme. The bridge exists so you can drive your producer over HTTP, and the conformance suite runs against it.

## Proving it

```
rimsky conformance claim-producer --endpoint grpc://localhost:9101 --check-observability
```

The suite drives the whole envelope. It checks that `Capabilities` answers and that `write_semantics_allowed` is non-empty; opens a synthetic claim and checks that `realized_write_semantics` is concrete and inside the envelope; opens a second and checks that byte-equal scopes carry identical semantics; drives each of `Commit`, `Abandon`, and `Release` on a fresh claim; drives each of the three twice on the same claim to prove idempotency; exercises `SplitScope` and `ScopesConflict` when you advertise them, checking that the sub-scope list returns every element with its partition key and payload preserved and its address field empty. When you advertise `WRITE_SEMANTICS_STAGED_ASYNC` it adds one more check: it opens a read-intent claim on a byte-equal scope while a read-write claim is open, and requires you to hand the reader its claim. Serializing readers behind writers fails that check — staged-async support means snapshot delegation or native multi-version reads, not a reader lease.

`--transport http` runs the same suite against your HTTP bridge. `--check-observability` needs gRPC; there is no HTTP+JSON path for it in the conformance kit. Add `--retention-test-seconds N` to drive a claim to terminal, wait, and check that `GetClaim` then answers `UNKNOWN`.
